scope: Single work unit for the root issue. ## Original definition (verbatim)

10. **FOS-000010 — Explain unsupported features and blocked dependencies.** **M, staged by resource type; depends on `FOS-000009`; §1–§2.** Feature filter predicates return bool, often at detailed feature/property checks; [setup:1270](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/cli/fossilize_replay.cpp#L1270) reduces this to “not supported.” Return feature/extension/property identifiers and relevant limits when known. Pilot compute, then graphics/ray-tracing/static objects. Link missing/failed parents or modules to blocked consumers rather than counting consumers as independent compiler faults. **Check:** one unsupported feature; one invalid module referenced by many pipelines; missing common-cache input; unknown pNext sType. Preserve existing support advice only where justified. Do not make “unsupported” a catch-all for parse, OOM or missing dependency failures.

   **Required automated success criteria — pending implementation:**

   - **Feature-filter unit tests per migrated resource type:** Known feature, extension, property-limit and unknown-sType rejections return the correct identifier and available observed/required values; supported controls succeed. Parse errors and OOM remain separate categories.
   - **Dependency-graph tests:** One failed shader/module or parent referenced by N pipelines yields one originating failure and N correctly linked blocked consumers, with zero creation calls for those unattempted consumers. Missing-common-cache cases identify a missing dependency without claiming the driver failed.

## Text warning volume — PR #75 follow-up

At the user's request, cap ordinary unsupported-object and blocked-dependency text warnings, show a few representative examples, and summarize affected replay work by the relevant cause: for example, “X pipelines could not be replayed because Y is not supported.” Preserve all original acceptance criteria above.

- Group by meaningful feature, extension, property/API boundary or unknown identifier, rather than individual pipeline hashes or every varying requested limit; retain relevant values and source identities in bounded examples. Keep unsupported, missing/failed dependencies, parse errors, OOM and driver failures distinct.
- Bound retained cause groups, example output and memory even for many distinct causes, with honest overflow counts. Totals remain correct after the example cap and under concurrent replay. State the summary's worker/attempt scope; do not imply cross-worker unique-item accounting.
- Replace duplicate legacy warnings for these same support/dependency failures, including detector/parser paths, so they cannot bypass the cap. Preserve unrelated error reporting, existing bool/non-replay callers, quiet-worker behavior, support policy and structured-event/outcome counts.
- Produce the summary once on ordinary completion/failure, including standalone replay without a structured-event writer. Success-only runs must not gain warning noise; hard process death must not be presented as a completed summary.
- Add Release-active automated checks of actual production text output: large repeated fanout, multiple meaningful causes and values, distinct-cause overflow, concurrency, representative identities, standalone/worker/quiet paths, duplicate-warning suppression and successful controls. Preserve the original full regression obligations. Native Windows verification remains user-waived and unverified.

11. **FOS-000011 — Expose discovery and selection completeness.** **M; depends on `FOS-000009`; §2.** [stream scanning:1200](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/fossilize_db.cpp#L1200) intentionally salvages truncated tails (E9). Database composites may omit unavailable inputs; whitelists/ranges and replay-cache checks change observable work. Return preparation/discovery metadata: requested/opened inputs, excluded inputs/items with policy, selected logical scope, truncation/read failures, complete/unknown discovery. Keep salvage behavior and report its limits. **Check:** intact empty archive versus truncated archive with zero retained entries; missing optional versus required subdatabase; filters and ranges. Known processed items cannot establish full coverage when unread scope is unknown. A caller may explicitly accept a recovered prefix, but the report must name that scope.

   **Required automated success criteria — pending implementation:**

   - **Database/discovery integration tests:** E9 reports incomplete discovery even with zero retained items, while an intact empty archive reports known complete empty scope. The intact prefix remains readable; required missing/unreadable inputs prevent full-scope success.
   - **Selection/policy table tests:** Ranges, whitelists, deliberately optional inputs and explicitly accepted recovered-prefix policy report the exact selected/excluded scope and policy. Unknown unread totals remain unknown, never zero or full coverage; excluded items are not counted as failures or successes.

## Original definition (verbatim)

12. **FOS-000012 — Reconcile final logical items across recovery attempts.** **M, split types/range-recovery if necessary; depends on `FOS-000009`, `FOS-000010`, `FOS-000011`; §2–§4.** Current atomics count activity and broad skips, while [condensed progress:71](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/fossilize_external_replayer.cpp#L71) explicitly clamps/weights counts and documents retry duplication. Preserve that UI estimate, but add authoritative accounting by selected `(tag, hash)` and attempt within a run/input scope. Distinguish selected work from extra dependencies and benchmark repetitions. Each selected item gets one final outcome; attempts retain their history. **Check:** duplicate/reordered messages, stale attempt failure after successful retry, one crash plus skipped culprit plus successful tail, unreported worker work. Do not infer exact successful counts by subtracting overlapping failure counters. Bound memory using range summaries/compact tables where possible; lost evidence must remain unknown.

   **Required automated success criteria — pending implementation:**

   - **Reconciliation model/property tests:** For a known selected set, every item has exactly one final outcome and final counts sum to that set. Permutations and duplicates of equivalent event histories yield the same final result; a stale failure cannot overwrite a newer authoritative success.
   - **Recovery and evidence-loss tests:** Failed attempt then complete retry succeeds with attempt history retained; skipped culprit plus successful tail remains incomplete. Lost reports retain unknown scope/counts. Extra dependencies, duplicate hashes across inputs and benchmark repetitions obey the declared identity rules without inflating selected-item counts.
   - **Bounded-state stress test:** Reconciliation of a generated large workload respects a documented state-size bound for the chosen representation; log sampling cannot alter authoritative accounting.
